alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ realized by the verse-initial For.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun he and nothing else; the relativizer stays with the participle. Rule 31 is not the case, no head noun being expressed.
The participle carries the supplied relativizer that under rules 7 and 32; headed on the lexical verb said.
Ordinary prohibitive μή aligned to not; rule 44 does not apply, this being no interrogative particle.

The subjunctive takes its imperative auxiliary Do under rule 9, discontinuously under rule 15 across the negative. Head on adultery under rules 17 and 91: commit is the empty support verb and adultery is what glosses μοιχεύω, as bear witness heads on witness. A head on commit is the competing reading and rests only on English syntax, which rule 17 refuses.
Adjunctive καί rendered also. Decided on the English alone, as rule 65 decides an intensifying καί: the ASV writes a word for it, so it is its own aligned unit.
Second prohibitive μή aligned to not.
Auxiliary Do rides with the subjunctive under rule 9, discontinuously across the negative; headed on the lexical verb kill.
Postpositive δέ rendered by the clause-initial Now.
Ordinary conditional εἰ aligned to if.
οὐ aligned to not in the ordinary way: no negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.

The inflected verb takes its supplied subject thou and the auxiliary dost under rule 9, the unit discontinuous across the negative under rule 15. Head on adultery under rules 17 and 91, matching s005; a head on commit is the competing reading.
φονεύεις rendered by the single finite killest; the subject carries over from the preceding clause and the ASV writes none here.
Perfect γέγονας takes its subject thou and the auxiliary art under rule 9; headed on the lexical become rather than the auxiliary, per rule 17.
Anarthrous παραβάτης with the supplied indefinite a as a rule 7 and 51 helper on the noun, no article competing.

νόμου is anarthrous, so the supplied the is a rule 7 helper on the noun rather than an article's determiner (rule 51), and the case preposition of rides with it; rule 21 is not in question, no article standing to anchor a determiner. Headed on law per rule 17.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged. Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units are needed, every source token having English in this verse.
s001/s003 follow rule 32 rather than rule 31: no head noun is expressed, so the article keeps only he and the participle keeps that said, headed on said.

The two 'commit adultery' units head on adultery under rule 17's support-verb clause and rule 91's operational test (commit carries no part of the μοιχεύω lexeme, as bear witness carries none of μαρτυρέω). A head on commit is the competing reading and is named in both units; it could rest only on English syntax, which rule 17 forbids.

The English do-support in Do not commit (t005) and dost not commit (t017) is licensed by the negation in English, but rule 9 places an auxiliary with the verb it belongs to, so both ride with their verbs and only not goes to μή/οὐ. That leaves s005, s009 and s013 discontinuous, which rule 15 permits and which absorbs no unrelated token.
s012 οὐ stays aligned: rules 41 and 59 empty a negator only where a negative indefinite follows that can carry the English negation alone, and none stands here.
s018 νόμου is anarthrous, so no article/noun split arises and the whole of of the law is one unit; rule 21's of the analysis applies only where a Greek article is present.
